questiontext.text:
UniCV prototype for Parsons problems in Python (based on python3_parsons_problem, with a new interface and a new grader). The student builds a program by putting the given code blocks in the right order and with the right indentation; the program is then run with each test case.

How to write a question

  1. Write the correct program in the Global extra field, one code block per line and indented as it must be. The interface shuffles the blocks: there is no need to shuffle or unindent them.
  2. Optionally add distractors: lines that end with #distractor (wrong blocks that are not needed). Lines that end with #given are already placed in the student's program and cannot be moved (useful to give a function header or the last print).
  3. To make one block of several lines, write them on one line separated by \n, e.g. if x > 0:\n print(x).
  4. Build the Answer with the same interface (the correct program) and add the test cases: Standard input and Expected output, or Test case code such as print(area(2, 3)) for a function.
  5. Save with Validate on save ticked: the answer must pass all tests. Twig all is not needed.

What the student gets

  • Two panes, Code blocks and Your program, with line numbers, syntax colours and indentation guides. The blocks are shuffled in a different order for each attempt.
  • Blocks are moved by dragging (mouse, pen or touch) or by clicking a block, which adds it at the end of the program. Each line has buttons ◀ ▶ (indentation), ↑ ↓ (move) and ✕ (back to the code blocks), and can also be handled with the keyboard.
  • A counter of lines and blocks left, a Help panel and a Start again button (with confirmation).
  • After Check, a line with a syntax or indentation error, or a return nested too deep, is marked in red with the message beside it, and no tests are run. Runtime errors show a short traceback with the line numbers of the student's program.

Limitations

  • The blocks of a question are its lines in Global extra; a block of several lines is written with \n as above.
  • Two blocks with exactly the same text are interchangeable.
  • With "grading": "order" the program must be exactly the answer (same blocks, same order, same indentation); other correct programs are not accepted.
  • The syntax colours are a simple approximation of Python's.
  • Students' answers are stored as the text of their blocks. If the blocks of a question are changed after students have answered it, the blocks that no longer exist cannot be restored: they get a message asking them to check their program or tell the teacher.

Differences from python3_parsons_problem

  • New interface without jQuery UI: line numbers, colours, indentation guides, a drop marker that shows where the block will go and at which indentation, buttons and keyboard for every action, works on touch screens, and errors marked on their line.
  • Simpler authoring: the program is written once, in Global extra; there is no need to paste it twice, shuffle, unindent or tick Twig all.
  • Given (fixed) lines with #given, an option to give the indentation (a line #indent: fixed in Global extra), and an option to grade by order instead of running ("grading": "order").
  • New grader: syntax and indentation errors are explained before running, each test is run separately (an error in one test does not spoil the others), there is a time limit per test (endless loops are reported) and hidden tests are supported. It needs no support files.
  • Fixed bugs of the original: an error in the syntax-colouring code (assignment to a constant) and the browser alert().

Note on input(): by default input() behaves as on the keyboard, so the prompt and the value read (followed by a new line) appear in the output and must be in the Expected output. For example, with n = int(input("n? ")) and input 4 the output starts with n? 4. Set echostandardinput to false to get plain Python behaviour.

Options in Global extra

  • #indent: fixed: a line with only this text anywhere in Global extra makes every block keep the indentation written there, so the student only chooses the order (no ◀ ▶ buttons). Without it, the student also chooses the indentation.

Template parameters (all optional)

  • grading (default "run"): "run" runs the program with the test cases; "order" compares it with the answer and says how many lines are in the right place (add one test case, which is not used).
  • echostandardinput (default true): see the note on input() above.
  • maxreturndepth (default none): the deepest level at which a return may be inside its function (1 = directly in the body), e.g. 1 to forbid a return inside a loop.
  • proscribedbuiltins (default ["exec", "eval", "open", "compile"]): built-in functions the program cannot use.
  • timeout (default 3): time limit in seconds for each test.
  • strictwhitespace (default true): if false, differences in spaces inside lines are ignored.
  • maxoutputlength (default 10000): longer outputs are cut.

Example: {"maxreturndepth": 1, "timeout": 2}

question.template:
"""Grader for the UniCV Parsons problem prototype (unicv_python3_parsons). The student's answer is the program built in the interface, stored as {"program": ["[[indent, text], [indent, text], ...]"]}: one pair per code block, in program order (a block may hold several lines, separated by \n). The grader rebuilds the program, checks it (empty, syntax and indentation errors, maxreturndepth) and then either runs every test case with it (grading "run", the default) or compares it with the question's answer (grading "order"). Errors that belong to one block are written in the feedback as , so that the interface can mark that block in red. """ import ast import builtins import html import io import json import signal import sys import traceback STUDENT_ANSWER = """{{ STUDENT_ANSWER | e('py') }}""" QUESTION_ANSWER = """{{ QUESTION.answer | e('py') }}""" TESTCASES = json.loads("""{{ TESTCASES | json_encode | e('py') }}""") ALL_OR_NOTHING = "{{ QUESTION.allornothing }}" == "1" IS_PRECHECK = "{{ IS_PRECHECK }}" == "1" try: PARAMS = json.loads("""{{ QUESTION.parameters | json_encode | e('py') }}""") except ValueError: PARAMS = {} if not isinstance(PARAMS, dict): # Twig encodes an empty set of parameters as [] PARAMS = {} GRADING = str(PARAMS.get('grading', 'run')).lower() ECHO_INPUT = PARAMS.get('echostandardinput', True) TIMEOUT = float(PARAMS.get('timeout', 3)) MAX_OUTPUT = int(PARAMS.get('maxoutputlength', 10000)) MAX_RETURN_DEPTH = PARAMS.get('maxreturndepth', None) STRICT_WHITESPACE = PARAMS.get('strictwhitespace', True) PROSCRIBED_BUILTINS = PARAMS.get('proscribedbuiltins', ['exec', 'eval', 'open', 'compile']) # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Reading the answer # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- def read_program(answer): """The list of (indent, text) blocks of an answer, or [] if it has none.""" try: data = json.loads(answer) raw = data.get('program', ['']) raw = raw[0] if isinstance(raw, list) else raw items = json.loads(raw) if raw else [] return [(max(0, int(indent)), str(text)) for indent, text in items] except (ValueError, TypeError, AttributeError): return [] def build_code(items): """The program's source code and, for each of its lines, the number (1-based) of the block it belongs to.""" lines, owner = [], [] for number, (indent, text) in enumerate(items, 1): for line in text.split('\n'): lines.append(' ' * (4 * indent) + line) owner.append(number) return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n', owner def place(lineno, owner): """(block number, line number) of a line of the program, or (None, None).""" if lineno and 1 <= lineno <= len(owner): return owner[lineno - 1], lineno if lineno and owner and lineno > len(owner): # e.g. a block expected after the last line return owner[-1], len(owner) return None, None # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Checks done before running # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- def return_depth_errors(tree, max_depth): """(line, message) for each return nested more than max_depth levels inside its function (1 = directly in the function's body).""" errors = [] compound = (ast.If, ast.For, ast.While, ast.With, ast.Try, ast.AsyncFor, ast.AsyncWith) def visit(node, depth): for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(node): if isinstance(child, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.Lambda)): continue if isinstance(child, ast.Return) and depth > max_depth: levels = 'level' if max_depth == 1 else 'levels' errors.append((child.lineno, f'return may not be indented more than {max_depth} {levels} in this question')) visit(child, depth + 1 if isinstance(child, compound) else depth) for node in ast.walk(tree): if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)): visit(node, 1) return errors def precheck_errors(items, code, owner): """A list of (block number, line number, message); the numbers may be None.""" if not items: return [(None, None, 'Your program is empty: move the code blocks into it.')] try: tree = compile(code, 'program.py', 'exec', ast.PyCF_ONLY_AST) except SyntaxError as err: kind = 'indentation error' if isinstance(err, IndentationError) else 'syntax error' return [place(err.lineno, owner) + (f'{kind} ({err.msg})',)] errors = [] if MAX_RETURN_DEPTH is not None: for lineno, message in return_depth_errors(tree, int(MAX_RETURN_DEPTH)): errors.append(place(lineno, owner) + (message,)) return errors def errors_html(errors, title): parts = [f"

{html.escape(title)}

    "] for block, lineno, message in errors: where = f'Line {lineno}: ' if lineno else '' parts.append(f'
  • {html.escape(where + message)}
    • ') parts.append('
') for block, lineno, message in errors: if block: parts.append(f'' f'{html.escape(message)}') return ''.join(parts) # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Running the tests # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- class TimeLimit(Exception): pass class OutOfInput(Exception): pass def on_alarm(signum, frame): raise TimeLimit() def forbidden(name): def stub(*args, **kwargs): raise NameError(f"'{name}' cannot be used in this question") return stub def run_one(program, testcode, stdin): """Run the compiled program and then the test code; return the output.""" out = io.StringIO() names = dict(vars(builtins)) real_input = builtins.input def echo_input(prompt=''): out.write(str(prompt)) line = sys.stdin.readline() if not line: raise OutOfInput() line = line.rstrip('\n') if ECHO_INPUT: out.write(line + '\n') return line def to_out(*values, sep=' ', end='\n', file=None, flush=False): out.write((sep if sep is not None else ' ').join(str(v) for v in values) + (end if end is not None else '\n')) names['input'] = echo_input names['print'] = to_out for name in PROSCRIBED_BUILTINS: if name != '__import__': names[name] = forbidden(name) scope = {'__name__': '__main__', '__builtins__': names} saved = sys.stdin, sys.stdout, sys.stderr sys.stdin, sys.stdout, sys.stderr = io.StringIO(stdin), out, out signal.signal(signal.SIGALRM, on_alarm) signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, TIMEOUT) try: exec(program, scope) if testcode.strip(): exec(compile(testcode, 'test', 'exec'), scope) except TimeLimit: out.write('\n*** Time limit exceeded (endless loop?) ***\n') except OutOfInput: out.write('\n*** input() was called but there is no more input data ***\n') except SystemExit: pass except BaseException: kind, value, tb = sys.exc_info() frames = [f for f in traceback.extract_tb(tb) if f.filename in ('program.py', 'test')] out.write('\nTraceback (most recent call last):\n' + ''.join(traceback.format_list(frames))) out.write(traceback.format_exception_only(kind, value)[-1]) finally: signal.setitimer(signal.ITIMER_REAL, 0) sys.stdin, sys.stdout, sys.stderr = saved builtins.input = real_input text = out.getvalue() if len(text) > MAX_OUTPUT: text = text[:MAX_OUTPUT] + '\n*** Output too long: cut ***\n' return text def normalise(text): lines = [line.rstrip() for line in text.rstrip().split('\n')] if not STRICT_WHITESPACE: lines = [' '.join(line.split()) for line in lines] return '\n'.join(lines).strip('\n') def run_tests(program, tests): has_code = any(t.get('testcode', '').strip() for t in tests) has_input = any(t.get('stdin', '').strip() for t in tests) header = ['iscorrect'] + (['Test'] if has_code else []) + (['Input'] if has_input else []) + \ ['Expected', 'Got', 'iscorrect', 'ishidden'] rows, got_marks, all_marks, hiding, hidden_failed = [header], 0.0, 0.0, False, False for test in tests: testcode, stdin, expected = test.get('testcode', ''), test.get('stdin', ''), test.get('expected', '') got = run_one(program, testcode, stdin) ok = normalise(got) == normalise(expected) mark = float(test.get('mark', 1) or 1) all_marks += mark if ok: got_marks += mark display = str(test.get('display', 'SHOW')).upper() hidden = hiding or display == 'HIDE' or (display == 'HIDE_IF_SUCCEED' and ok) or \ (display == 'HIDE_IF_FAIL' and not ok) if hidden and not ok: hidden_failed = True if not ok and str(test.get('hiderestiffail', '0')) in ('1', 'True', 'true'): hiding = True row = [ok] + ([testcode.rstrip()] if has_code else []) + ([stdin.rstrip()] if has_input else []) + \ [expected.rstrip(), got.rstrip('\n'), ok, hidden] rows.append(row) if all_marks == 0: fraction = 1.0 elif ALL_OR_NOTHING and got_marks < all_marks: fraction = 0.0 else: fraction = got_marks / all_marks return fraction, rows, hidden_failed # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Main # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- def main(): items = read_program(STUDENT_ANSWER) code, owner = build_code(items) outcome = {'fraction': 0.0} errors = precheck_errors(items, code, owner) if errors: outcome['prologuehtml'] = errors_html(errors, 'Your program cannot run yet') return outcome if IS_PRECHECK: outcome['fraction'] = 1.0 outcome['prologuehtml'] = "

Passed: the program has no syntax or indentation errors.

" return outcome if GRADING == 'order': wanted = [(indent, text.strip()) for indent, text in read_program(QUESTION_ANSWER)] mine = [(indent, text.strip()) for indent, text in items] if mine == wanted: outcome['fraction'] = 1.0 outcome['prologuehtml'] = "

All the lines are in the right order and correctly indented.

" else: right = sum(1 for a, b in zip(mine, wanted) if a == b) extra = ' Some of the blocks you used are not needed.' if len(mine) > len(wanted) else '' missing = ' Some blocks are still missing.' if len(mine) < len(wanted) else '' outcome['prologuehtml'] = ("

Not yet right

" f"

{right} of {len(wanted)} lines are in the right place and correctly indented.{extra}{missing}

") return outcome tests = [t for t in TESTCASES if str(t.get('testtype', '0')) != '1'] program = compile(code, 'program.py', 'exec') fraction, rows, hidden_failed = run_tests(program, tests) outcome['fraction'] = fraction if len(rows) > 1: outcome['testresults'] = rows outcome['showdifferences'] = True if hidden_failed: outcome['epiloguehtml'] = "
One or more hidden tests failed.
" return outcome print(json.dumps(main()))
